hints: Notice that $P_{in}$ is the total power supplied to the television and $P_{out}$ is only the useful sound and light power.
Recall that efficiency compares useful output to total input, not wasted energy to input.
Check which fraction $P_{out}$ over $P_{in}$ or $P_{in}$ over $P_{out}$ must be less than 1 for a real device.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantities: total power in is $P_{in}$ and useful power out as sound and light is $P_{out}$.
State the governing rule: $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{\text{useful output}}{\text{total input}}$.
For power, this can be written directly as $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{P_{out}}{P_{in}}$.
Note that $P_{in} - P_{out}$ represents wasted thermal power, so a ratio using it does not give efficiency.
Therefore the required ratio is $P_{out}$ divided by $P_{in}$. This is option A.

options.A: Efficiency is useful output power $P_{out}$ divided by total input power $P_{in}$.
options.B: This is the fraction of input power wasted as heat, since $P_{in} - P_{out}$ is wasted power, not useful power.
options.C: This inverts the ratio and would give a value greater than 1, but efficiency cannot exceed 1.
options.D: This divides useful power by wasted power $P_{in} - P_{out}$, not by total input power.
